taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-13, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1340.2 | 1.08 | 1.08
2 | 2148.3 | 1.38 | 2.46
3 | 5322.7 | 1.26 | 3.72
4 | 18475.7 | 0.33 | 4.05
5 | 19320.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-13, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station T-13, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation at T-13 resolves five layers with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: 1340.2 Ω·m (0–1.08 m), 2148.3 Ω·m (1.08–2.46 m), 5322.7 Ω·m (2.46–3.72 m), 18475.7 Ω·m (3.72–4.05 m), and 19320.3 Ω·m (basal layer, unbounded). This steadily rising resistivity trend indicates a transition from a shallow, more conductive surface layer to increasingly resistive material at depth, consistent with a progression from weathered/soil cover into more competent, possibly fractured or compact bedrock.

Applying the standard three-layer letter convention, each successive triplet (1-2-3, 2-3-4, 3-4-5) yields "A" (r1 < r2 < r3), giving the full curve code AAA, equivalent to the single-letter designation "A". This matches the on-file classification of A-type for this station, and no discrepancy was found between the tabulated resistivity values and the assigned curve type.

{"curve_type_stated": "A", "label_issue_flagged": false}
